title: Beef, Flank, Steak, Boneless, Choice, Raw

content.title: About
content.content: Flank steak is a cut taken from the lower abdominal muscles of the cow (the flank). It is classified as “choice”, indicating a high level of marbling and quality. This boneless, raw steak is commonly used for quick, high‑heat cooking to retain its juiciness and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flank steak is considered one of the tougher cuts, so it is often sliced against the grain to improve tenderness.
Traditionally, flank steak is a staple in Mexican cuisine, especially in fajitas.
In the United States the term “London broil” is sometimes applied to flank steak, although it can refer to other cuts as well.
Because of its texture, flank steak absorbs marinades well, making it popular for barbecue.
Raw flank steak can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, but freezing is recommended for longer storage.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flank steak supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Meat naturally contains creatine, which can help improve strength and endurance during exercise.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli or Salmonella and should be cooked thoroughly.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Although a “choice” cut, flank steak still contains saturated fats that should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Hyperuricemia
items.content: Large portions of red meat can raise uric acid levels, which may be problematic for people with gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marinate the flank steak for at least 30 minutes, then sear it quickly over high heat to the desired doneness (commonly medium‑rare). Let it rest 5–10 minutes and slice thinly against the grain. It works well in salads, tacos, sandwiches, or served as a standalone steak.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw beef refrigerated at 0–2 °C in an airtight container for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a vacuum‑sealed bag at –18 °C; it will keep for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen steak in the refrigerator before cooking.
